classifiedFinding.title: collectReward is permissionless: any wallet can re-anchor rewardPerSecond at trivial cost, indefinitely extending the depletion tail

classification.assetImpact: Stakers receive far less than the advertised depletion rate as a griefer keeps the rate-recompute near zero. Reward tokens are not stolen but their effective distribution is impaired, leaking value to nobody (parked in rewardBalance) or to far-future entrants.
attackPath: 1. Yield-accumulator funds collectReward(real_amount); rewardPerSecond set high.
2. Griefer calls collectReward(1) every block; each call re-anchors rewardPerSecond against the same (slightly increasing) rewardBalance over the full depletionDuration.
3. Effective rewards-per-second is suppressed near zero; stakers receive a tiny fraction of advertised yield.
4. Total griefer cost: 1 wei × N blocks plus gas — trivial on L2.
classification.likelihood: medium — requires sustained griefer; rational only if griefer derives value from suppressing yield (e.g., short on protocol, holds competing position)
classification.assumptions: No access control on collectReward (verified by reading code); attacker has trivial budget; V1 rate-recompute behavior (acknowledged known issue)
classification.externalRequirements: Griefer wallet with rewardToken balance ≥ 1 wei per call

classifiedFinding.justification: Protocol function (reward distribution) is impaired by a permissionless surface. Distinct from the V1 rate-recompute KI: this is the access-control gap that amplifies it. Separately remediable (whitelist the yield-accumulator OR enforce minimum funding amount). Value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements (griefer cost ≥ epsilon). Fits the Medium criteria.
classifiedFinding.notes: Sanitizer hinted potential-medium. Classifier agrees. Could be argued down to Low/QA given the underlying V1 behavior is acknowledged, but the access-control angle is fresh and the remediation is clean (single access-control line). Holding at Medium.
